newsitem.title: USA: Glaxo in Phase III trials on HIV drug.
newsitem.headline: Glaxo in Phase III trials on HIV drug.

text.p: Glaxo Wellcome Plc has begun a Phase III clinical trials for an inhibitor intended to treat HIV infection and AIDS in adults, Glaxo Welcome's partner, Vertex Pharmaceuticals Inc, said Thursday.

The trials for the inhibitor, known as 141W94/VX-478, as well as advanced clinical studies underway or planned by Glaxo are intended to support filing for market approval of the drug in the United States and other countries, Vertex said.
The drug is a second generation HIV inhibitor being developed by Glaxo, Kissei Pharmaceutical Co Ltd, and Vertex, it said.
A Phase III clinical trials of the drug in children is expected to begin in the coming weeks, it added.
The Phase III privotal clinical trial should generate important clinical data," said Joshua Boger, president and chief executive officer of Vertex.
The study is expected to involve about 240 HIV-positive adudlts and will be conducted in about 30 trial sites in the U.S., Canada and Europe, Vertex said.

It added that Glaxo Wellcome's double-blind, placebo-controlled trial is designed to evaluate the tolerability and efficacy of the drug through its combination with AZT and 3TC, compared to the double combination of AZT and 3TC,
AZT or zidovudine and 3TC or lamivudine, are both AIDS drugs. Both trademarks belong to the Glaxo Wellcome group.
